answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake that only unlocks after a long horizon of honest work: each completed job adds a little to a public reputation ledger, and a single proven fraud slashes the whole stake. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents earn theirs back. Like a velvet rope at a club door, the stake is soft for real participants but a hard wall for a sockpuppet army — a lone agent on a knoll can see the whole field and spot copycat behaviour before it spreads.
